newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-UCBSA CHANGES MIND OVER STREAK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-UCBSA CHANGES MIND OVER STREAK.

text.p: The United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA) has reversed a decision to allow Zimbabwe fast bowler Heath Streak to appear as a guest player for Mashonaland in their Standard Bank Cup semi-final against Natal in Durban on April 18.

Streak, who represents Matabeleland province in his country's domestic competition, was initially given clearance a month ago by UCBSA to turn out for a depleted Mashonaland side for the Kingsmead encounter.
But UCBSA managing director Ali Bacher said on Wednesday that this decision would no longer apply.
"Heath Streak will not be permitted to play for Mashonaland as he is not an overseas player with them," Bacher told Reuters.
"While, from a cricketing point of view, his inclusion would strengthen a weakened side, the principle is wrong and it would not be in the interests of the competition.
"The official request for Streak to play for Mashonaland in fact came from the Zimbabwe Cricket Union and I conveyed our decision to their president Peter Chingoka this morning. He accepts it fully."
The initial clearance for Streak to play for Mashonaland came from the UCBSA's playing affairs committee which, at the time, felt his bolstering of the side would be in the interests of good cricket.

"Considering that they (Mashonaland) have lost a huge complement of their players for the Kingsmead match, the feeling was that any player strengthening their side was something to be supported," UCBSA director of umpiring Brian Basson told Reuters on Wednesday.
"Natal's quarter-final match against Kenya in Durban last month was a bit of a disappointment and, from a crowd point of view, it would be desirable to have a closer-fought semi-final at Kingsmead."

Mashonaland, who beat Eastern Province in Port Elizabeth to book their place in the tournament's semi-finals, will be without five key players for their clash with Natal - four Zimbabwe test cricketers and one English county player.

Former Zimbabwe captain Andy Flower (Oxford) and Grant Flower (Epsom College) are committed to coaching contracts in England, Zimbabwe player-coach Dave Houghton is already back in Britain coaching English county Worcestershire and wrist-spinner Paul Trang is Kent's new overseas player for 1997.
Mashonaland's 1996-97 overseas player James Kirtley has returned to home county Sussex for the up-coming cricket season.
